title: PathChat-SegR1: Reasoning Segmentation in Pathology via SO-GRPO
claim: A frozen-plus-adapted pathology encoder, language model and mask decoder chain together so a text query yields a reasoned segmentation mask.
layout: 3 panels: top pretraining and adapter insets, main pipeline left-to-right below, frozen/trainable icons
description: A three-part architecture diagram. Panel (a), top left, shows pretraining of the MedSAM image encoder. Two stain-varied histology patches are masked and passed through a transformer block (Layer Norm, Multi-head Attention, MLP) to a decoder. The figure marks MAE reconstruction losses and a distillation loss between the two branches. Panel (b), top right, zooms into the Seg-Adapter, a residual bottleneck with Down, GELU, Up and Scaling blocks. A legend marks frozen modules with snowflakes and trainable ones with flames. Panel (c), the main pipeline, takes a pathology image and a text query. The image goes through the MedSAM encoder with Seg-Adapters. The Ruipath encoder, projector, LLM with LoRA and text embeddings produce a [SEG] token. A projector passes that token to the mask decoder, which outputs an overlaid mask. A reasoning text answer sits at the lower right. Cyan marks frozen modules and peach marks trainable ones.
caption: PathChat-SegR1 architecture overview.
abstract: Segmentation in pathology image requires handling out-of-domain tissue morphologies and new pathologies beyond training distributions, where traditional closed-set segmentation approaches fail to generalize. Reasoning segmentation enables zero-shot generalization via prompting with text queries. However, existing reasoning segmentation models face three barriers when applied to pathology: (1) the vision encoder lack pathology-specific knowledge and robustness to staining variations, (2) the large language model (LLM) backbone for reasoning fails to identify whether it has gathered sufficient semantic context to trigger the segmentation output, and (3) no reasoning segmentation benchmarks and datasets exist for pathology analysis. Consequently, we introduce PathChat-SegR1, a reasoning segmentation model built upon pathology-specific vision encoders trained with a novel stain-invariant self-distillation for robust pathology image representations. Moreover, we propose Segmentation-Optimized GRPO (SO-GRPO), a reinforcement learning method specifically for reasoning segmentation that learns to determine optimal segmentation timing based on accumulated reasoning context. Finally, we construct a pathology-specific reasoning segmentation benchmark of 118,667 triplets of pathology image, ground-truth mask, query, and reasoning chain including both public and private pathology images. Zero-shot evaluation on pathology images with out-of-domain morphologies/pathologies shows 61\% improvement over state-of-the-art segmentation models.
